tasks.title: Learning Objectives
tasks.explainer:
Today we will learn how to:

- combine background image settings with the `background` shorthand
- create `radial-gradient()` backgrounds
- create `linear-gradient()` backgrounds
- control gradient direction with keywords and angles

The key shorthand pattern is:

```css
background: url("image.jpg") no-repeat center/cover;
```

subtasks.title: Background Shorthand - 1
subtasks.explainer:
# What Is Shorthand?

A **shorthand** property is one CSS property that accepts several related values.

Instead of writing four separate background declarations, we can combine them into one `background` declaration:

```css
background: url("/assets/html-3-7/skiing.jpg") no-repeat center/cover;
```

The slash matters: `center` is the position and `cover` is the size.

subtasks.title: Background Shorthand - 2
subtasks.explainer: Match each shorthand part to its job.

subtasks.title: Background Shorthand - 3
subtasks.explainer: Which shorthand correctly centres the image and makes it cover the div?

options.feedback: In background shorthand, the size comes after the position with a slash before it.
`background-image` only chooses the image. The shorthand property is `background`.
The usual pattern is image, repeat, then position/size.

subtasks.title: Radial Gradients - 1
subtasks.explainer:
# What Is a Gradient?

A **gradient** is a smooth change from one colour to another.

CSS can generate gradients for us. A gradient behaves like an image, so we can place it in `background-image`.

```css
background-image: radial-gradient(red, yellow);
```

A `radial-gradient()` starts near the middle and spreads outward.

subtasks.title: Radial Gradients - 2
subtasks.explainer:
# Create a Radial Gradient

Add a radial gradient to `.circle` using two colours of your choice.

A radial gradient needs at least two colour values separated by a comma:

```css
background-image: radial-gradient(red, yellow);
```

A radial gradient can include a shape and a starting point.

Change the `.circle` gradient so it starts from a corner:

```css

```

You can choose different colours if you want.

subtasks.title: Linear Gradients - 1
subtasks.explainer:
# Linear Gradients

A `linear-gradient()` changes colour along a straight line.

By default, it runs from top to bottom.

```css
background-image: linear-gradient(red, yellow);
```

Like a radial gradient, it can be used as a `background-image` value.

subtasks.title: Linear Gradients - 5
subtasks.explainer:
# Angle Values

We can also control gradient direction with an angle.

Angles use the unit `deg`, which means degrees.

```css
background-image: linear-gradient(45deg, red, yellow);
```

Changing the number changes the direction of the colour change.

tasks.title: Debug the Shorthand
tasks.explainer:
Why might this shorthand not behave as expected?

```css
background: url("skiing.jpg") no-repeat center cover;
```

options.text: It is missing the slash before `cover`.
The image URL is always wrong.
options.feedback: The image URL is not the issue here.
`center` is a valid position value, but the size needs to be separated from it.

tasks.explainer:
# Create a Promo Card

Create a promo card for a game, film, sport, or place.

Your design must include:

- a `.poster` with a `background` shorthand image
- a `.circle` with a `radial-gradient()`
- a `.rectangle` with a `linear-gradient()` using an angle
- at least one heading inside the poster

Choose your own colours. The checks focus on the CSS techniques, so your teacher can review the design choices.

subtasks.title: Recap - 1
subtasks.explainer:
- `background` is shorthand for several background settings.
- `center/cover` means the position is `center` and the size is `cover`.
- `radial-gradient()` spreads out from a point.
- `linear-gradient()` changes colour along a line.
- `deg` controls a gradient angle.
